purpose: Semantic data dictionary defining entities, attributes, relationships and controlled vocabulary used by the EU AI Act Compliance Management System™. Extends v1.0.2 by adding: (1) explicit bidirectional relationships with cardinalities between entities, (2) a crosswalk mapping each logical entity to the schema.org @type actually deployed in this site's JSON-LD, and (3) the site-content entities (pages, glossary terms, FAQ items) that the original v1.0.2 model did not cover.

Organization.definition: Legal entity operating AI systems and responsible for compliance activities.

AI_System.definition: Machine-based system capable of generating outputs such as predictions, recommendations, decisions or content.

AI_Use_Case.definition: Business scenario where an AI system is applied.

Module.definition: EU AI Act compliance domain — one of the 10 operational modules.

Document.definition: Controlled compliance document — one of 7 types per module.

Incident.definition: Operational event affecting AI system compliance or performance.

Page.definition: A single published URL on eu-ai-act-ready.eu. New in v1.1.0 — connects the logical compliance model above to the actual deployed website.

GlossaryTerm.definition: A defined term used throughout the EU AI Act Compliance Management System, published on the Glossary page.

FAQItem.definition: A single question/answer pair, published visibly on a page and mirrored in that page's FAQPage JSON-LD.

relationships.note: One organization can operate many AI systems; each AI system is operated by exactly one organization in this model.
One AI system may be applied across multiple use cases.
Many AI systems can share one risk category; each AI system has exactly one active classification at a time.
One organization works through all 10 modules; a module definition itself is shared/reused across organizations (module content is the same, module STATUS is per-organization).
Each module contains exactly 7 documents (one per document_type). This is a fixed 1:7 cardinality, not open-ended.
A single document (particularly an Evidence-type or Register-type document) can reference multiple underlying evidence records.
One AI system may have zero or many incidents logged against it over its lifecycle.
An incident's investigation and resolution is documented by one or more evidence records.
One requesting organization's data (firm name, responsible person) populates many generated document pages/files via the Generator.
A page may display zero or many FAQ items; each FAQ item is authored for exactly one page (no cross-page sharing in the current implementation).
Pages link to each other via breadcrumb, footer quick links, and in-content navigation — self-referencing many-to-many relationship.
A glossary term (e.g. 'AI System', 'High-Risk') may be relevant to multiple modules; a module's documents may use multiple glossary terms.

schema_org_crosswalk.purpose: Maps each logical entity above to the schema.org @type actually emitted in this site's live JSON-LD, so the correspondence between the conceptual model and the deployed markup is explicit and auditable rather than assumed.

known_gaps: GlossaryTerm entities exist as visible content on glossary.html but are not yet marked up individually with schema.org DefinedTerm/DefinedTermSet — this is the one real remaining gap between the logical model and deployed markup.

The AI_System, AI_Use_Case, Risk_Category, Incident entities describe the RRVI *product's* data model (what a customer's own compliance data looks like once they use the system) — they are not expected to appear in this site's own JSON-LD, since they describe customer data, not site content. Listed here for completeness of the logical model only.
